> Operator request, 2026-08-07: *"record the user experience with an eye for consistency across screens and platforms... then review the code files for maintainability... then a review of documentation."* Reviewed jointly with the independent Antigravity/Gemini auditor; **where we disagreed, the disagreement is recorded rather than averaged.**
## 1. Modal sizing — the finding is DIVERGENCE, not breakage
The auditor called this *"15 functional blockers — users cannot see 15 modal workflows on macOS"*. 🚨 **That is wrong, and the way it is wrong is the actual finding.**
Measured across the 31 views presented via `.sheet`:
| Convention | Count |
| --- | --- |
| `.macSheet(minWidth:minHeight:)` | 11 |
| `.macFormSheet(minHeight:)` | 4 |
| Raw `#if os(macOS)`  • `.frame(…)` | **15** |
| Nothing — and correctly so (`VStack`, has intrinsic height) | 1 |
**No sheet is currently broken.** The 15 raw-frame sheets are properly guarded to macOS and work.
⭐ **But three conventions exist for one job, and that is why this bug class keeps recurring.** Establishing the above took four attempts: a grep for `macSheet` missed the raw frames; a grep for `frame(minWidth` missed `macFormSheet`; a platform-guard check mis-parsed `#if` nesting and produced two false positives. **Each attempt produced a confident, different, wrong answer.** If the state cannot be determined with one search, the next person adding a sheet cannot determine it either — which is exactly how seven sheets once shipped collapsed.
**Rule to adopt:** every `.sheet`-presented view ends in `.macSheet` or `.macFormSheet`. No raw `#if os(macOS) + .frame`. Then one grep answers the question, and a missing modifier is visible in review.
## 2. Affordance divergence — the operator's complaint, made specific
*"Functions that are menu options on one screen are huge buttons on others."* Confirmed. Destructive actions currently appear as toolbar ⋯ items, inline `Button(role: .destructive)` rows, and full-width buttons; tools launch from Settings rows, toolbar buttons and toolbar menus.
⚠️ **The accessibility failure is the one that produced a real bug**, not the cosmetic variance. The video ⋯ menu grew past the screen at a large text size and took `Delete Video…` with it — present, rendered, unreachable, and indistinguishable from removed. A menu is not a scrollable list; item count is a correctness concern.
**Rules to adopt:**
- A destructive action lives **last in the ⋯ menu**, after a divider — never a standalone button.
- **A ⋯ menu holds at most five top-level items.** Beyond that, group into submenus. Assume every label wraps to three lines.
- Library-wide tools live in **Settings**; record-scoped actions live in that record's **⋯**. The video inspector already follows this; it is the pattern to copy.
## 3. Maintainability — where the auditor is right, and where it is not
**Agreed — genuinely doing too much:**
- **`LibraryStore.swift`**** (2,450 lines).** Schema DDL for v1–v30 plus every query in the application. The seam is clean and the split is mechanical: `SchemaMigrator` for the migrations, then `LibraryStore+Assets` / `+Profiles` / `+Tags` / `+Edges` / `+Audits`. ⚠️ `dbQueue` is private to the file by deliberate decision, so extensions must live in the same module and that privacy needs re-checking — the split is not free.
- **`ContentView.swift`**** (1,549 lines)** holds ~25 `@State` sheet booleans. The auditor's enum-routing suggestion is right, and there is now direct evidence for it: **two navigation bugs this session** came from hand-rolled routing that forgot the compact-layout path.
**Disagreed — the auditor guessed:**
It declared `ProfileGraphHeaderView` *"FINE — dynamic canvas drawing, custom geometry calculations, header animations"*. **There is no canvas drawing, no geometry maths and no animation in that file.** It reads a profile, renders an identity block, a lineage block and pivot bubbles for four entity kinds. The verdict may be right; the reasoning is invented, and an invented reason is not evidence. It is a **1,029-line view that branches on entity kind throughout** — the honest reason to leave it alone is that its branches were the fix for studios showing hair colour, and re-splitting them now would undo work that is not yet device-verified.
## 4. Documentation — the weakest surface
### App `README.md` — five weeks stale (6 July), materially wrong
| Claim | Reality |
| --- | --- |
| *"Metadata graph — actors, studios, tags, series; entity profiles"* | Describes profiles only. **Six edge tables, migrations v27–v30, and the entire graph do not appear.** |
| `LibraryCore` = scanning, persistence, thumbnails, tag normalisation | Omits the plugin architecture, matching, enrichment, audits, batch policies — most of the package |
| *"Covers **`LibraryStore`**, **`LibraryScanner`**, and the tag utilities"* | **1,146 tests** across graph audits, career arc, edge attributes, temporal hierarchy, batch policies |
| Roadmap: *"☐ Manual playlists with drag-and-drop ordering"* | **Shipped.** `playlists` / `playlist_items` tables and `PlaylistDetailView` exist |
| — | The plugin architecture and two-library federation are **absent entirely** |
### Plugin `README.md` — wrong about its own integration
- *"Implements **`ActorMetadataProvider`** and (later) **`VideoMetadataProvider`**"* — the video half shipped in `ef2de39`, and a **studio** provider now exists too.
- *"Video metadata — blocked on a spike (D11)"* — no longer true.
- 🚨 *"The consuming build adds this package as an untracked local path dependency"* — **it does not.** The app **symlinks individual source files** into `ViLM/LocalPlugins/ActorVideoMetadata/`. This was discovered the hard way: new plugin files compiled in the package and were invisible to the app until symlinks were added by hand. A README describing the wrong integration mechanism costs an hour the first time someone believes it.
### In-app help — an incomplete list presented as complete
`HelpContent.settings` **enumerates the maintenance tools item by item**. **Zero** of the seven tools added this session appear: Studio Health, Impossible Data, Match All Studios, Repair Studio Spelling, Remove Series Names, Connect the Graph, Age-at-Release filtering.
One stale entry was already corrected mid-session — help pointed at a *"Danger Zone section"* removed three weeks earlier, and the operator spent real time looking for it. That is the cost of this surface being wrong, demonstrated.
### Notion — the most current surface, with gaps of my own making
Every spec is Approved and carries an implementation-status table. But **three changes shipped with no spec entry at all**: `StudioSpellingCleanupView`, the Connect-the-Graph list/link work, and the actor-batch-by-name fix. ⚠️ Recorded here because the traceability rule is mine to follow too, and I did not.
Also: no spec is marked **Implemented**, which is correct — that state requires operator device verification, and most of this is a day old.
## The three changes worth making first
1. **Standardise sheet sizing on the two helpers.** Cheap, mechanical, and it makes the recurring bug class greppable. Not urgent — nothing is broken today.
2. **Rewrite both READMEs.** The plugin one actively misleads about integration; the app one omits the last two months of architecture. Highest ratio of harm to effort.
3. **Add the seven missing tools to in-app help**, and adopt the rule that a tool ships with its help entry — the Danger Zone incident is what this costs when skipped.
The `ContentView` and `LibraryStore` splits are real but should follow device verification of the current work, not precede it.
